title: Sapling

stage.name: Sapling
stage.description: A thin woody trunk forms and carries water up to the crown.

intro: The young tree gets stronger, inside and out.

questions.prompt: Which tissue carries water up from the roots?
questions.why: Xylem moves water upward. Phloem moves sugar from the leaves to where it's needed.

questions.prompt: Match each part of the trunk to its job.
questions.why: Xylem and phloem are the tree's plumbing, and bark is its protective skin.

questions.prompt: A trunk gets thicker because a thin layer called the cambium adds new wood each year.
questions.why: The cambium adds new wood on the inside and new bark on the outside.

questions.prompt: Bark protects a young tree. What protects a relationship during disagreements?
questions.why: Contempt and shutting down are among the clearest warning signs for couples. A gentle start keeps a disagreement about the problem, not the person.

talk: When you disagree, what helps you feel heard?
